chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalah, from Rifa'ah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, restored health to Ayoub (peace be upon him), he looked at the Children of Israel who had sown (crops), so he raised his gaze to the sky and said: 'My God and my Master, Your servant Ayoub, the afflicted, You granted him health, and he has no place to sow anything, and this is a plantation of the Children of Israel.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Ayoub, take a handful from your rosary (or prayer beads), and sow it.' And his rosary contained salt in it. So Ayoub (peace be upon him) took a handful from it and sowed it, and this lentil came out. And you call it chickpeas, and we call it lentils.'
ai.seo_question: What is the origin of lentils according to Shia hadith narrations about Prophet Ayoub?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the miraculous nature of Prophet Ayoub’s (AS) recovery by linking his spiritual devotion to agricultural bounty, specifically identifying the origin of lentils (or chickpeas) through a divine command. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of using such narratives to illustrate the interconnection between prophetic piety, divine favor, and the natural world, serving as a sign of God’s power over creation.
